AI-assisted course construction

Bring a complete course into the Studio.

Use an AI assistant to organize your source material into a Course Creator Studio course file. The Studio then checks the structure, accounts for the source material, preserves anything uncertain for review, and creates a normal editable course only when the import is safe.

01No silent dropping.
Source content must be included, preserved for later, deliberately excluded, or placed in review.
02The AI organizes; the Studio checks.
The Studio does not guess what a damaged or incomplete course file meant.
03Imported means editable.
Once created, the course uses the same modules, lessons and elements as a course built by hand.

Start here

What are you starting with?

Choose the closest match for the material you already have. Your AI assistant prepares a course file that you upload here. Pick a more careful option whenever you are unsure; it is safe, it just takes an extra step.

Standard

A short outline, notes, or a few pages

Best for straightforward written material with no important visual layout. The AI organizes it into an editable course in one pass.

Most careful

A long guide, manual, or multi-part course

Best when missing a section would matter. First make a checked source record, then turn that same record into your editable course.

Visual material

Important tables, charts, diagrams, or worksheets

Use this even for a short document when visual relationships or exact cells matter. Uncertain visuals stay visible for your review instead of being guessed.

Workbooks and handouts

A facilitator guide, workbook, or handout

Best for guided exercises, worksheets, and supporting handouts. It organizes clear source material into editable lessons and preserves uncertain material for review.

Not sure which one? Choose the long-guide option when your material has several chapters, important details, or anything you would not want accidentally shortened or missed.

About AI quality: Results vary by AI tool and source format. More capable models usually handle long documents and complex visuals more reliably; free tools can work well for shorter, simpler material. Always review the imported course before sharing it with learners.

The fix prompt appears only when the Studio finds a problem in an uploaded file.

How courses save—and what “Saved on this device” means

The Studio saves course projects inside the browser being used on that computer. There is no online account and no automatic cloud synchronization.

  • Opening the Studio in another browser, browser profile or computer may show a different or empty course library.
  • Clearing browser or website data can remove locally saved projects.
  • Keep the Studio file and downloaded backups in a normal computer folder you control.
Best practice: Download a Studio backup after any substantial work and before clearing browser data, changing computers, deleting courses or updating the builder file.
How many courses can be kept in one Studio?

There is no fixed course-count limit. Capacity depends mostly on how many embedded documents and images the projects contain.

Course typePractical working range
Mostly written lessons and links100+ courses
Several small PDFs or images per courseAbout 20–40 courses
Several large files near the 5 MB upload limitAbout 5–10 courses

For a consistent experience across different computers and browsers, plan around approximately 25 active, normally sized courses. Archive older work rather than treating browser storage as permanent unlimited storage.

How to back up, remove and restore course projects
  1. Select Download Studio backup below.
  2. Save the JSON file somewhere easy to identify, such as a folder named “Course Backups.” Include the date in the filename.
  3. Confirm that the backup file exists before deleting anything from the builder.
  4. Remove older course projects from My Courses when the active library becomes crowded or file-heavy.
  5. To restore a backup later, return here and select Import / Restore Backup. A single-course backup is added as a new independent course; a complete Studio backup asks before replacing the Studio currently stored on this device.
Important: A complete Studio backup is a snapshot of the entire editable Studio. Restoring a full Studio backup replaces the Studio currently stored on this device after confirmation. Importing a single-course backup does not replace existing courses—it restores that course as a new independent copy.

A client ZIP or learner HTML file is not an editable backup. Use Back up course in Share Course for an individual-course JSON backup, or Download Studio Backup in Settings for the complete Studio.

How to deliver a finished course to a learner
  1. Open the correct project and confirm that every learner-ready lesson is marked Published.
  2. Use Preview to inspect the portal and test its lesson navigation and links.
  3. Open Share Course and select Send to client.
  4. The Studio creates a clearly named ZIP containing START-HERE instructions and the course file.
  5. Attach the ZIP to an email or place it in a shared cloud-storage folder and send the download link.
  6. The included START-HERE file tells the learner how to extract the ZIP, open the course and back up progress.

The course itself works offline. Embedded resources remain inside the HTML. YouTube videos and external webpage links still require internet access.

If email blocks HTML attachments: place the file in a ZIP folder or upload it to Google Drive, Dropbox or another file-sharing service and send the download link.
What the learner can—and cannot—do
  • The learner can open lessons, move between lessons, mark work complete and return to the course dashboard.
  • Progress is saved in that learner’s browser on that device.
  • The learner cannot edit lessons, see drafts, access creator settings or open other course projects.
  • If the creator changes the course later, a new client package must be sent to the learner.
  • Progress does not automatically transfer between browsers, devices or replacement portal files.
Simple file organization for creators

Create one main folder called Offline Course Studio, then use three subfolders:

  • 01 Studio: the protected master builder HTML.
  • 02 Editable Backups: dated all-projects JSON backups.
  • 03 Learner Courses: finished client packages organized by course, cohort or learner.

Use clear filenames with the course name and date. Never overwrite the only backup copy.

Course-building definitions

Plain-language meanings for the terms used throughout the Studio.

ModuleA main section of a course. Think of it like a chapter that contains lessons.
LessonOne learning step inside a module.
Learning blockOne piece of a lesson, such as text, an image, practice activity, reflection or quiz.
Course BlueprintA ready-made course starting point you can copy and customize.
PrerequisiteEarlier material a learner must complete before another module or lesson unlocks.
Completion ruleWhat a learner must do before a lesson can be marked complete.
PublishedVisible in the learner course. Draft and Hidden lessons stay inside the Studio.
Knowledge checkA short question used to confirm understanding during a lesson.
